questions.subject: science
options: Two or more substances chemically bonded together
Two or more substances mixed but not chemically joined
questions.answer: Two or more substances mixed but not chemically joined
questions.hint: Can it be separated without a chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: In a mixture the substances are physically combined, not bonded. They keep their own properties and can be separated by physical methods (filtering, evaporating, distilling). Compounds need chemical reactions to separate.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which separation technique would best separate sand from water?
questions.hint: Sand is insoluble — what would catch it?
questions.explanation: Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid. The sand stays as residue on the filter paper; the water passes through as filtrate.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: When filtering, what name is given to the liquid that passes through the filter paper?
questions.explanation: Filtrate = the liquid that passes through. Residue = the solid left on the paper. The two terms get muddled — remember 'filtrate flows'.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How would you separate salt from a salt-water solution if you only want the salt?
questions.hint: Filtering won't work — the salt is dissolved. You don't need the water back.
questions.explanation: Salt is soluble so it passes through filter paper. To get the salt, evaporate the water away by heating in an evaporating basin. The salt is left as crystals.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which technique separates a liquid from a solution and keeps BOTH the solvent (e.g. water) and the solute (e.g. salt)?
questions.hint: Evaporation loses the water. We want it back.
questions.explanation: In distillation the solution is heated; the solvent boils off, then condenses back into a liquid in the condenser. You collect pure water AND have the salt left in the original flask.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which technique would best separate ethanol from water (which boil at different temperatures)?
questions.hint: Both are liquids that mix together — you need a method that uses boiling points.
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation uses a fractionating column to separate liquids with different boiling points. Ethanol (78°C) boils first and is collected before water (100°C).
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Chromatography is used to separate which kind of mixture?
questions.hint: Think about putting a felt-tip dot on filter paper and dipping it in water.
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates components of a mixture (often coloured) by how far they travel up paper in a solvent. Different dyes move different distances based on solubility.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: On a chromatogram, which type of dye travels the FURTHEST up the paper?
options: The most soluble in the solvent used
The least soluble in the solvent
questions.answer: The most soluble in the solvent used
questions.hint: Solubility — the more soluble, the more easily it's carried by the moving solvent.
questions.explanation: More soluble dyes dissolve more easily in the solvent and travel further up the paper. Less soluble dyes stay closer to the starting line.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In a salt-water solution, what is the SOLUTE?
questions.explanation: The solute is the substance dissolved (salt). The solvent is what dissolves it (water). Together they form a solution.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the SOLVENT in a sugar-water solution?
questions.explanation: Water is the solvent — it dissolves the sugar (the solute). Water is called the 'universal solvent' because it dissolves so many substances.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What does it mean if a substance is 'insoluble' in water?
questions.explanation: Insoluble = doesn't dissolve. Sand and chalk are insoluble in water. Soluble substances (like sugar and salt) do dissolve.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A student has a mixture of sand, salt, and water. Which sequence of techniques would separate all three?
options: Filter (to remove sand), then evaporate the water (to get salt)
questions.answer: Filter (to remove sand), then evaporate the water (to get salt)
questions.hint: Get rid of the insoluble bit first, then deal with the dissolved bit.
questions.explanation: Filter first — sand stays on the paper (insoluble), salt water passes through. Then evaporate that filtrate — water leaves as vapour, leaving salt crystals.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How could you separate a mixture of iron filings and sand?
questions.explanation: Iron is magnetic; sand isn't. A magnet picks up the iron filings, leaving the sand behind. This works because the substances have different physical properties.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Seawater contains salt dissolved in water. Which separation technique would you use to produce DRINKABLE water from seawater?
questions.hint: You want to keep the water, not the salt.
questions.explanation: Distillation evaporates water from seawater and condenses it back as pure liquid — the salt is left behind. Used in desalination plants in places like the Middle East.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A black ink is tested using paper chromatography. Three coloured spots appear above the original line. What can you conclude?
options: The ink is a pure substance
The ink is a mixture of at least three different dyes
The ink contains exactly three atoms
questions.answer: The ink is a mixture of at least three different dyes
questions.hint: If it was pure, only one spot would appear.
questions.explanation: A pure substance gives one spot in chromatography. Three spots mean three different dyes were mixed to make the black ink — they separate because they travel at different speeds.
questions.source: CHS Y7 Science KM, Summer Term — Separating Techniques
